source_text: Icrrur secundum magnitudinem non est cognoscere Deum ; impossibile est enim mensurari Patrem ; secundum autem dilectionem ejus, hee est enim que nos per Verbum ejus perducit ad Deum, obedientes ei semper discimus quoniam est tantus Deus, et ipse est qui per semetipsum constituit, et elegit, et adornavit, qui est secundum nos. Et nos igitur cum his que continentur ab eo, factisumus. Et hic est de quo Scriptura ait; Ht plasmavit Deus hominem, limum terre accipiens, et insufflavit in faciem ejus Jjlatum vite. Non ergo angeli fecerunt, nos, nec nos plasmaverunt, nec angeli potuerunt imaginem facere Dei, nec alius quis preter Verbum Domini, nec virtus longe absistens a Patre uniNec enim indigebat horum Deus ad faciendum quie ipse apud se preefinierat fieri, quasi ipse suas non haberet manus. Adest enim ei semper Verbum et Sapientia, Filius et Spiritus, per quos, et in quibus omnia libere et sponte fecit, ad quos et loquitur, dicens: Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram; ipse a semetipso substantiam creaturarum, et exemplum factorum, et figuram in mundo ornamentorum accipiens. 2. Bene igitur pronuntiavit scriptura que dicit: Primo omnium crede, quoniam unus est Deus, qui omnia constituit, et consummavit, et fecit ex eo quod non erat, ut essent omnia: Omnium capax, et qui a nemine capiatur. Bene autem et in prophetis Malachias ait: Nonne unus Deus qui constituit nos? Nonne Pater unus est omnium nostrum ? Consequenter autem et Apostolus ait: nus Deus, inquit, Pater, qui super omnes, et in omnibus nobis. Similiter autem et Dominus: Omnia mihi, inquit, tradita sunt a Patre meo; manifeste ab eo qui omnia fecit: non enim aliena, sed In omnibus autem nihil subtractum est: et propter hoe idem est Judex viventium et mortuorum, habens clavem David: ' aperiet, et nemo claudet : claudet, et nemo aperiet. Nemo enim alius poterat nec in ccelo, nec in terra, nec sub terra aperire paternum librum, nec videre eum, nisi agnus qui occisus est, et sanguine suo redemit nos, ab eodem, qui omnia Verbo fecit et Sapientia adornavit, accipiens omnium potestatem, quando Verbum caro factum est, ut quemadmodum in ccelis principatum habuit Verbum Dei, sic et in terra haberet principatum, quoniam homo justus, gui peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus; principatum autem habeat eorum que sunt sub terra, ipse primogenitus mortuorum factus, et ut videant omnia, quemadmodum preediximus, suum Regem: et ut in carnem Domini occurrat paterna lux, et a carne ejus rutila veniat in nos, et sic homo deveniat in incorruptelam, circumdatus paterno lumine. 3. Et quoniam Verbum, id est Filius, semper cum Patre erat, per multa demonstravimus. Quoniam autem et Sapientia, est Spiritus, erat apud eum ante omnem constitutionem, per Salomonem ait: Deus sapientia fundavit terram, paravit Sensu ejus abyssi eruperunt, nubes autem manaverunt ros. Et rursus autem: Dominus creavit me principium viarum suarum in opera sua, ante swcula fundavit me, initio antequam terram faceret, priusqguam abyssos constitueret, et priusquam procederent fontes aquarum, antequam montes confirmarentur: ante omnes autem colles genuit me. Et iterum: Cum pararet coelum, eram cum illo,* et cum firmos faceret fontes abyssi, quando fortia faciebat fundamenta terra, eram apud eum aptans. Eyo eram cui adgaudebat, quotidie autem letabar ante faciem ejus in omni tempore, cum letaretur orbe perfecto, et jocundaretur in filiis hominum. 4. Unus igitur Deus, qui Verbo et Sapientia fecit et ° adaptavit omnia: hic est autem Demiurgus, qui et mundum hune attribuit humano generi, qui secundum magnitudinem quidem ignotus est omnibus his qui ab eo facti sunt: nemo enim investigavit altitudinem ejus, nec veterum qui quieverunt, nec eorum qui nune sunt, secundum autem dilectionem cognoscitur semper per eum, per quem constituit omnia. ejus Dominus noster Jesus Christus, qui novissimis temporibus homo in hominibus factus est, ut finem conjungeret principio, id Et propterea prophetee ab eodem Verbo proest, hominem Deo. pheticum accipientes charisma, preedicaverunt ejus secundum carnem adventum, per quem commixtio et communio Dei et hominis secundum placitum Patris facta est, ab initio preenunciante Verbo Dei, quoniam videbitur Deus ab hominibus, et conversabitur cum eis super terram, et colloqueretur, et adfuturus esset suo plasmati, salvans illud, et perceptibilis ab eo, et liberans nos de manibus omnium odientium nos, hoc est, ab universo transgressionis spiritu: et faciens nos servire sibi in sanctitate et Justitia omnes dies nostros, uti complexus homo Spiritum Dei, in gloriam cedat Patris.
pass_a_gloss: It is not possible to know God according to magnitude; for it is impossible to measure the Father; but according to his love, this is what leads us to God through his Word, obeying him we always learn that God is so great, and he is the one who establishes and chooses and adorns, who is according to us. And therefore we, with the things that are contained by him, have been made. And this is what Scripture says: God formed man, taking clay of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life. Therefore, angels did not make us, nor did they form us, nor could angels make the image of God, nor anyone else except the Word of the Lord, nor a power far removed from the Father. For God did not need these things to do what he had predetermined to do, as if he did not have his own hands. For the Word and Wisdom, the Son and Spirit, are always present with him, through whom and in whom he freely and willingly made all things, to whom he also speaks, saying: Let us make man in our image and likeness; he himself taking from himself the substance of creatures, and the example of things made, and the form of ornaments in the world. Scripture has rightly declared, saying: First of all, believe that there is one God, who established and completed and made all things from what did not exist, so that all things might be: capable of all things, and not capable of being grasped by anyone. And also in the prophets, Malachi says: Is it not one God who established us? Is it not one Father of all of us? And consequently, the Apostle also says: There is one God, the Father, who is over all and in us all. Similarly, the Lord says: All things have been handed over to me by my Father; clearly by him who made all things: for nothing has been taken away: and because of this, he is the judge of the living and the dead, having the key of David: he will open, and no one will shut: he will shut, and no one will open. For no one else could open the book of the Father, neither in heaven nor on earth nor under the earth, nor see it, except the Lamb who was slain and redeemed us with his blood, from him who made all things by the Word and adorned them by Wisdom, receiving all power, when the Word became flesh, so that just as the Word of God had primacy in heaven, so also he might have primacy on earth, because the just man, who did not commit sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth; and he might have primacy over the things that are under the earth, he himself having become the firstborn of the dead, and so that all things might see their King, as we have previously said: and so that the paternal light might encounter the flesh of the Lord, and the red light might come to us from his flesh, and so man might become incorruptible, surrounded by the paternal light. And since the Word, that is, the Son, was always with the Father, we have demonstrated this through many things. And since Wisdom, that is, the Spirit, was with him before all establishment, Solomon says: God founded the earth by Wisdom, the abysses burst forth by his sense, and the clouds flowed with dew. And again: The Lord created me, the beginning of his ways, for his works, before the ages he founded me, in the beginning before he made the earth, before he established the abysses, and before the springs of water proceeded, before the mountains were confirmed: before all the hills he begot me. And again: When he prepared the heaven, I was with him, and when he made the strong foundations of the abyss, when he made the strong foundations of the earth, I was with him, adapting. I was the one in whom he delighted, and I rejoiced daily before his face at all times, when he rejoiced in the perfect orb, and was delighted in the sons of men. Therefore, there is one God, who made and adapted all things by the Word and Wisdom: and this is the Demiurge, who also attributed this world to the human race, who according to magnitude is indeed unknown to all who have been made by him: for no one has investigated his height, neither the ancients who have rested, nor those who are now: but according to love, he is always known through him, through whom he established all things, our Lord Jesus Christ, who in the last times became man among men, so that he might join the end to the beginning. And therefore, prophets, receiving the prophetic gift from the same Word, predicted his coming according to the flesh, through which the mixture and communion of God and man was made, according to the will of the Father, the Word of God having previously announced that God would be seen by men, and would converse with them on the earth, and would be present with his creation, saving it, and being perceived by it, and liberating us from the hands of all who hate us, that is, from the spirit of all transgression: and making us serve him in holiness and justice all our days, so that man, having received the Spirit of God, might give glory to the Father.

pass_b_english: We cannot know God by measuring his magnitude, for it is impossible to measure the Father; but we are led to God through his Word according to his love, and by obeying him we always learn how great God is. He is the one who establishes, chooses, and adorns all things in relation to us, and so we ourselves have been made together with everything he contains. This is what Scripture says: God formed the human being from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). Therefore angels did not make us, nor did they form us, nor could angels make the image of God, nor anyone else except the Word of the Lord, nor any power far removed from the Father. God did not need such helpers to do what he had predetermined, as if he lacked his own hands. For the Word and Wisdom, the Son and Spirit, are always present with him, and through them and in them he freely and willingly made all things. He also speaks to them, saying, "Let us make man in our image and likeness," himself drawing from himself the substance of creatures, the pattern of things made, and the form of the world's ornaments.

Scripture has rightly declared: "First of all, believe that there is one God, who established and completed and made all things from what did not exist, so that all things might be: capable of all things, and not capable of being grasped by anyone." The prophet Malachi also says: "Is it not one God who established us? Is it not one Father of all of us?" (Malachi 2:10). And consequently the Apostle says: "There is one God, the Father, who is over all and in us all" (Ephesians 4:6). Similarly the Lord says: "All things have been handed over to me by my Father" — clearly by him who made all things, for nothing has been taken away. Because of this he is the Judge of the living and the dead, holding the key of David: "he will open, and no one will shut; he will shut, and no one will open." No one else could open the Father's book, neither in heaven nor on earth nor under the earth, nor even see it, except the Lamb who was slain and redeemed us with his blood from him who made all things by the Word and adorned them by Wisdom. He received all authority when the Word became flesh, so that just as the Word of God held primacy in heaven, so also he might hold primacy on earth — because the righteous man who committed no sin, in whose mouth no deceit was found — and primacy over the things under the earth, having become the firstborn of the dead. And so all things might see their King, as we have previously said; and so the paternal light might meet the flesh of the Lord, and radiant light might come to us from his flesh, and so humanity might become incorruptible, wrapped in the Father's light.

We have demonstrated through many passages that the Word, that is, the Son, was always with the Father. And since Wisdom, that is, the Spirit, was with him before all creation, Solomon says: "By wisdom the Lord founded the earth; by understanding he established the heavens; by his knowledge the deeps broke open, and the clouds dropped down dew" (Proverbs 8:22-31). And again: "The Lord created me at the beginning of his work, the first of his acts of old. Ages ago I was set up, at the first, before the beginning of the earth. When there were no depths I was brought forth, when there were no springs abounding with water. Before the mountains had been shaped, before the hills, I was brought forth" (Proverbs 8:22-31). And again: "When he established the heavens, I was there; when he drew a circle on the face of the deep, when he made firm the skies above, when he established the fountains of the deep, when he assigned to the sea its limit, when he marked out the foundations of the earth, then I was beside him, like a master workman, and I was daily his delight, rejoicing before him always, rejoicing in his inhabited world and delighting in the children of man" (Proverbs 8:22-31).

Therefore there is one God, who made and ordered all things by the Word and Wisdom. This is the Demiurge, who also assigned this world to the human race. According to his magnitude he is unknown to all who have been made by him, for no one has searched out his height — neither the ancients who have rested, nor those who are now. But according to love he is always known through him through whom he established all things: our Lord Jesus Christ, who in the last times became man among men, so that he might join the end to the beginning. And therefore the prophets, receiving the prophetic gift from the same Word, predicted his coming in the flesh, through which the mingling and communion of God and humanity was accomplished according to the Father's good pleasure. The Word of God had previously announced that God would be seen by humans, would converse with them on earth, would be present with his creation, saving it, being perceived by it, and liberating us from the hands of all who hate us — that is, from the spirit of all transgression — and making us serve him in holiness and justice all our days, so that humanity, having received the Spirit of God, might give glory to the Father.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Scripture citations in Pass B (Genesis 2:7, Malachi 2:10, Ephesians 4:6, Proverbs 8:22-31) correctly identify the content of the Latin quotes. The translation of the Wisdom/Solomon section (Proverbs 8) correctly handles the multiple clauses and the complex structure of the Latin text.
